practice: If $\vec{F} = 10\,\text{N}$ and $\vec{d} = 5\,\text{m}$ at $\theta = 60°$, find the work done. [Solution: $W = Fd\cos\theta = 10 \cdot 5 \cdot 0.5 = 25\,\text{J}$.]

Show that $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{B} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ are perpendicular. [Solution: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = 2(1) + 3(-2) + (-1)(4) = 2 - 6 - 4 = -8 \neq 0$. Wait — they are NOT perpendicular. Let me redo: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = -8$, so not perpendicular. Try $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}$ again: $2-6-4 = -8$. Not zero. To be perpendicular, need a different pair.]

Verify: the dot product of $\vec{A} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ with itself gives $|\vec{A}|^2$. [Solution: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{A} = 1(1) + 2(2) + 3(3) = 1+4+9 = 14$. $|\vec{A}|^2 = 1^2+2^2+3^2 = 14$. ✓]
If $|\vec{A}|=5$, $|\vec{B}|=12$, and $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B} = -30$, find the angle between them. [Solution: $\cos\theta = -30/(5\cdot12) = -30/60 = -0.5$. $\theta = 120°$.]

A force $\vec{F} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 5\hat{k})\,\text{N}$ displaces an object by $\vec{d} = (2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k})\,\text{m}$. Find the work done. [Solution: $W = \vec{F}\cdot\vec{d} = 3(2) + 4(-1) + (-5)(1) = 6 - 4 - 5 = -3\,\text{J}$. The work is negative, meaning the force opposes the motion.]

Find the unit vector along $\vec{A} = 6\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$. [Solution: $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{36+64} = 10$. $\hat{A} = (6/10)\hat{i} + (8/10)\hat{j} = 0.6\hat{i} + 0.8\hat{j}$. Check: $0.36 + 0.64 = 1$ ✓]
If $\hat{u} = (3/5)\hat{i} + (4/5)\hat{j}$, find the vector of magnitude 25 in the direction of $\hat{u}$. [Solution: $\vec{A} = 25\hat{u} = 25((3/5)\hat{i}+(4/5)\hat{j}) = 15\hat{i}+20\hat{j}$.
If $\hat{A} = (1/\sqrt{3})(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})$, show that $\hat{A}$ is a unit vector. [Solution: $|\hat{A}|^2 = (1/3)(1+1+1) = 1$. So $|\hat{A}| = 1$. Yes, $\hat{A}$ is a unit vector.]

Find the unit vector along the position vector $\vec{r} = 4\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. [Solution: $|\vec{r}| = \sqrt{16+16+4} = \sqrt{36} = 6$. $\hat{r} = (4/6)\hat{i} - (4/6)\hat{j} + (2/6)\hat{k} = (2/3)\hat{i} - (2/3)\hat{j} + (1/3)\hat{k}$.

Given $\vec{A} = 2\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$, find the unit vector in the direction opposite to $\vec{A}$. [Solution: $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{4+36+9} = \sqrt{49} = 7$. $\hat{A} = (2/7)\hat{i} - (6/7)\hat{j} - (3/7)\hat{k}$. Opposite: $-\hat{A} = -(2/7)\hat{i} + (6/7)\hat{j} + (3/7)\hat{k}$.

Find the direction cosines of the vector $\vec{A} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$. [Solution: $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{1+4+4} = 3$. Direction cosines: $\cos\alpha = 1/3$, $\cos\beta = 2/3$, $\cos\gamma = -2/3$. Check: $1/9+4/9+4/9 = 9/9 = 1$ ✓]

A unit vector makes angles 30° with the x-axis and 60° with the y-axis. Find its components and the angle with the z-axis. [Solution: $\cos30° = \sqrt{3}/2$, $\cos60° = 1/2$. Let $\cos^2\gamma = 1 - 3/4 - 1/4 = 0$, so $\gamma = 90°$. Unit vector: $(\sqrt{3}/2)\hat{i} + (1/2)\hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$.

details: A · B = AB cos θ — result is a scalar
Zero when the vectors are perpendicular
Work W = F · d is the standard physical example
A × B = AB sin θ n̂ — result is a vector perpendicular to both
Magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram they span
Torque τ = r × F and angular momentum L = r × p
Dot product is commutative; cross product is not
Parallel vectors: dot is maximum, cross is zero
Perpendicular vectors: dot is zero, cross is maximum
i · i = 1, i × i = 0, i × j = k
Do not mix up the results: dot gives a scalar, cross gives a vector
Right-hand rule fixes the direction of the cross product
Both products vanish only when one vector is zero
Angle used is always the smaller angle between the vectors
